header.co_column_assumption: The column headed 'CO initial ambient composition' is treated as carbon dioxide (CO2). The PSI file does not say so; this is an assumption, to be confirmed by a chemist (DOB-51).
header.si_note: Generated by pipeline/flame_temperature/build.py, a script written with SI assistance (Claude Code, Anthropic). The humans chose the idea and the method.

steps.added_gas: none; carbon dioxide 0.05 to 0.70 step 0.05; helium 0.05 to 0.45 step 0.05; nitrogen is the rest
steps.d0_mm: 6 values evenly spaced across the FLEX range: [1.1, 1.81, 2.53, 3.24, 3.96, 4.67]
steps.left_out: positions where oxygen plus added gas is above 1

header.nearest: up to 5 real tests of the same fuel as [flex_test, distance]; distance = sqrt(sum of squared differences each divided by its scale); scales {'ceiling_temperature_k': 50.0, 'log10_heat_spreading': 0.1, 'd0_mm': 0.5}
header.no_test_near: if the nearest real test differs by more than 75.0 K in ceiling temperature the position has no prediction (a proposal, to be tuned)
header.prediction: gradient-boosted trees (the fitted link), trained once on all eligible tests

model_fails_here.label: model fails here
model_fails_here.text: Temperature alone does not explain helium (R2 -0.34). Outside reviewers point to transport. Our transport term reaches only R2 0.16.
model_fails_here.applies_to: every row whose added_gas is helium
model_fails_here.source: flex_checks.json, check carry_over_helium (straight line trained on tests without helium, scored on the methanol helium tests; the transport term is the heat-spreading speed)
